content:
The Boss’ “Streets of Minneapolis (Radio Mix)” — an anti-ICE protest song released in response to the president’s deadly immigration crackdown — has been nominated in the Best Rock Song category.

Springsteen released the music just four days after federal agents shot and killed Alex Pretti during a protest in January, slamming “King” Trump, his “federal thugs” and officials such as then-Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem and immigration hard-liner Stephen Miller.

In a social media post at the time, the Boss dedicated the song to both Pretti and Renee Good, the Minneapolis mother of three who was fatally shot by a federal agent that same month, as well as “our innocent immigrant neighbors.”

The Trump White House wasn’t happy about the song, which a spokesperson called “irrelevant” and “inaccurate” despite its debut at No. 1 on Billboard’s Digital Songs Sales chart the week it dropped.

Springsteen performed the song for Minnesotans at a benefit show organized by Rage Against the Machine’s Tom Morello shortly after its release.

In March, he played it again at a “No Kings” rally in St. Paul and later opened with the number during his Minneapolis tour stop with the E Street Band.

Springsteen could take home a Grammy for the song on Sunday, Feb. 7.

The Grammy nod arrives less than two weeks after Springsteen reminded election officials of their sworn “oath” to the Constitution ahead of Election Day as the president attempted to undermine public confidence in the midterms.

Springsteen has become a familiar focus of Trump’s attacks. In one Truth Social meltdown, the president described him as “a pushy, obnoxious JERK” and “dried out ‘prune’” after the rock icon called out his “corrupt, incompetent, racist, reckless and treasonous administration” during his Minneapolis tour stop.
